title: Charge-sharing-resistant advanced-node storage latches
open: Preserve latch data after multi-node charge collection from high-LET particle strikes while keeping practical area, delay, and power. Validate protection across strike angles, voltage, temperature, and realistic physical layouts.
status: Charge sharing has challenged scaling for decades; 2025 heavy-ion tests of 14-nm FinFET flip-flops found interleaved redundancy effective, while conventional DICE protection degraded at high LET.
why: Nominal logical redundancy need not survive physically correlated disturbances.
key_works: Hai-song Li et al. (2025), [*Investigation of DFF cells SEU effect for 14 nm bulk silicon FinFET technology irradiated by heavy ions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115857).

title: NEM relay contacts with stable loaded-switching lifetimes
open: Develop relay contacts retaining low resistance and repeatable release through prolonged switching of realistic capacitive loads. Quantify and suppress the competing effects of adhesion, wear, oxidation, and microwelding at small contact forces.
status: Central since 2000s NEM logic proposals; 2026 shock/vibration tests preserved mechanical function but found contact-related electrical variability and gold-coating wear. Mechanical survival alone does not establish switching lifetime.
why: Contact degradation can defeat the energy advantage of essentially zero off-state leakage.
key_works: Ivan Marozau et al. (2026), [*Mechanical shock and vibration testing of volatile and non-volatile nanoelectromechanical switches*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115980).

title: Buried EUV-mask phase-defect inspection
open: Detect, localize, and assess the printability of buried multilayer mask defects at production throughput, including defects obscured by patterned absorbers or pellicles.
status: Nanoscale optical detection and phase-sensitive techniques have progressed for over a decade; a 2013 NIST study demonstrated useful defect discrimination, not exhaustive production inspection.
why: Avoids repeating one invisible mask defect across many wafers.
key_works: Attota and Jindal (2013), [“Through-focus scanning optical microscopy for defect inspection of EUV masks”](https://www.nist.gov/publications/through-focus-scanning-optical-microscopy-defect-inspection-euv-masks).

title: Fast conformal deposition in deep closed-end features
open: Obtain uniform thickness and composition throughout increasingly deep structures without exposure and purge times that make deposition uneconomic.
status: ALD is already highly conformal; the unresolved scaling trade-off couples precursor transport, sticking, depletion, and radical recombination, systematized by Cremers and colleagues in 2019.
why: Supports reliable capacitors, memory channels, and three-dimensional gate stacks.
key_works: Cremers, Puurunen, and Dendooven (2019), [“Conformality in atomic layer deposition: Current status overview of analysis and modelling”](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5060967).

title: Glitch-power prediction across workloads and technologies
open: Predict energy from narrow pulses and hazards at large-design speed, including correlated input timing and realistic workloads, without a transistor-level simulation of every transition.
status: A 2024 study improved cell-specific pulse filtering in 32 nm simulations; accurate transfer across libraries, operating points, and large heterogeneous designs remains the target.
why: Makes power budgets and optimization reflect physical switching activity.
key_works: Villegas and Vourkas (2024), [“A Gate-Level Power Estimation Approach with a Comprehensive Definition of Thresholds for Classification and Filtering of Inertial Glitch Pulses”](https://doi.org/10.3390/jlpea14030041).

title: Transferable and reproducible learned chip placement
open: Establish when learned placers outperform strong conventional baselines on genuinely unseen designs and technologies, including training cost, post-route metrics, and repeated runs.
status: Mirhoseini et al. reported successful deployment in 2021; independent open assessments and the 2024 addendum show why evaluation protocol and transfer claims need explicit evidence.
why: Distinguishes reusable design intelligence from benchmark-specific optimization.
key_works: Mirhoseini et al. (2021), [“A graph placement methodology for fast chip design”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03544-w); Cheng et al. (2023), [“Assessment of Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11014).

title: Masking proofs that survive physical implementation
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Connect composable leakage-security proofs to measured CMOS behavior including glitches, unequal delays, coupling, and process variation, with affordable implementation overhead.
status: Robust probing models solved important formal subproblems; 2024 analysis demonstrates why eliminating glitches alone does not settle delay-induced leakage.
why: Gives cryptographic hardware guarantees that better match fabricated circuits.
key_works: Faust et al. (2017/2018), [“Composable Masking Schemes in the Presence of Physical Defaults and the Robust Probing Model”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/711); Müller, Lammers, and Moradi (2024), [“A Deep Analysis of two Glitch-Free Hardware Masking Schemes SESYM and LMDPL”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/035).

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave electrically injected group-IV laser
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Demonstrate a room-temperature, continuously electrically driven GeSn/SiGeSn laser coupled into a useful on-chip waveguide, with efficient, sustained operation.
status: Pursued since the 1990s; Seidel and colleagues demonstrated electrical continuous-wave lasing in 2024, limited to 35 K. Optical pumping and pulsed electrical operation establish partial feasibility.
why: Completes a group-IV optical source platform without separately assembled III–V gain chips.
key_works: Seidel et al. (2024), [*Continuous-wave electrically pumped multi-quantum-well laser based on group-IV semiconductors*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54873-z).
aliases: Electrically pumped silicon-compatible laser; group-IV laser temperature problem.

title: Manufacturable Pockels photonics with stable interfaces
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Produce heterogeneous electro-optic photonics with simultaneously low optical loss, low drive voltage, high bandwidth, uniform wafer performance, and stable bonded interfaces over service life.
status: Accelerated during the 2010s. Wang and colleagues demonstrated wafer-scale lithium-tantalate photonics in 2024, extending the options beyond lithium niobate; production-scale multimaterial yield and qualification remain combined challenges.
why: Adds efficient modulation to silicon-based communication and sensing chips.
key_works: Wang et al. (2024), [*Lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuits for volume manufacturing*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07369-1).

title: Lifetime lead containment after photovoltaic module damage
open: Demonstrate lead capture that remains effective after decades of weathering and realistic combinations of cracking, fire, flooding, and recycling, without sacrificing performance or economical manufacture.
status: A concern since the 2010s. Chen and colleagues substantially reduced lead release from damaged mini-modules with ion-exchange resins in 2020; lifetime and failure-scenario validation remains broader.
why: Enables safer deployment and end-of-life handling of lead-containing absorbers.
key_works: Chen et al. (2020), [*Trapping lead in perovskite solar modules with abundant and low-cost cation-exchange resins*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-020-00716-2).

title: Durable narrow-bandgap tin–lead perovskite junctions
open: Stabilize complete tin–lead photovoltaic junctions against self-doping, ionic redistribution, interfacial reactions, and oxidation under simultaneous heat and illumination, without losing narrow-bandgap efficiency.
status: A persistent 2010s–2020s problem. Rombach and colleagues showed in 2025 that dominant degradation pathways change with the hole-transport material; structurally stable absorbers can still produce deteriorating devices.
why: Enables durable all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics.
key_works: Rombach et al. (2025), [*Disentangling degradation pathways of narrow bandgap lead-tin perovskite material and photovoltaic devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58489-9).

title: Eliminating the kesterite voltage deficit
open: Suppress the bulk and interface losses behind kesterite's voltage deficit without introducing compensating defects or sacrificing manufacturable phase purity.
status: Open since the 2000s. Magnesium-assisted ordering produced 14.9%-efficient certified cells in 2025; defect activity and ordering kinetics remain intertwined.
why: Enables high-performance thin-film photovoltaics based on relatively abundant constituent elements.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025 online; 2026 issue), [*Vacancy-enhanced cation ordering via magnesium doping to enable kesterite solar cells with 14.9% certified efficiency*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01902-w).

title: Unambiguous non-Abelian Majorana operations in semiconductor hybrids
open: Demonstrate noncommuting exchange or equivalent measurement-only operations on semiconductor–superconductor Majorana modes, while excluding ordinary Andreev-state explanations and establishing a protected operating regime.
status: Pursued since 2010-era nanowire proposals. Microsoft Azure Quantum's 2025 parity-readout experiment explicitly allowed trivial and topological interpretations; parity measurement alone is not non-Abelian braiding.
why: Tests a proposed protected quantum-computing platform's physical basis.
key_works: Microsoft Azure Quantum and Aghaee et al. (2025), [*Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2).

title: Predicting coupled chemical degradation in blue OLEDs
open: Predict blue OLED luminance decay and failure products from competing electron-, exciton-, and mixed-carrier reactions without individually fitting each device lifetime.
status: Open for decades. Kim combined calculations, control devices, and mass spectrometry in 2023 to identify electron-assisted degradation in iridium emitters; prediction across materials and conditions remains unresolved.
why: Guides durable emitter design beyond empirical lifetime screening.
key_works: Kim et al. (2023), [*Critical role of electrons in the short lifetime of blue OLEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-43408-7).

title: High-brightness narrowband blue OLEDs without triplet accumulation
open: Maintain narrow deep-blue spectra and efficiency at sustained high brightness while suppressing trapping, triplet accumulation, annihilation, and chemical damage in sensitized emitters.
status: Pursued since the 2010s. Fan shifted molecular orbital energies in 2025, obtaining 13-nm emission bandwidth and approximately 20% efficiency at 1,000 cd/m²; high-brightness lifetime remains challenging.
why: Improves colour-pure, power-efficient displays under demanding luminance requirements.
key_works: Fan et al. (2025), [*Stable narrowband blue OLEDs by modulating frontier molecular orbital levels*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60172-y).

title: Comparable lifecycle inventories per good die
open: Publish auditable energy, water, chemical, and emissions inventories normalized to yielding functional dies, including equipment utilization, process yield, packaging, and uncertainty.
status: Lifecycle frameworks and virtual-fab models exist; imec's 2025 account explicitly notes dependence on yield, utilization, die size, and other assumptions.
why: Allows meaningful comparison of fabrication routes and design choices.
key_works: imec (2025), [“How can we reduce environmental impact in chip manufacturing?”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/how-can-we-reduce-environmental-impact-chip-manufacturing).

title: Predictive charged-defect energetics
open: Predict defect formation free energies and charge-transition levels with transferable uncertainty estimates, including localized states, competing geometries, and realistic chemical potentials. Success requires blind agreement with independently identified defects across semiconductor families.
status: A decades-old problem; finite-size corrections and hybrid functionals substantially improved calculations, but defect-specific validation remains necessary.
why: Makes doping and carrier-lifetime engineering less empirical.
key_works: C. Freysoldt et al. (2014), [First-principles calculations for point defects in solids](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.253).

title: Multimode anharmonic nonradiative capture
open: Calculate defect capture rates when multiple vibrational modes, anharmonicity, tunnelling, and strong electronic coupling act simultaneously. Establish experimentally validated criteria for when single-coordinate approximations fail.
status: Decades old; 2014 calculations quantitatively described selected GaN and ZnO defects, leaving broader multimode and anharmonic cases unresolved.
why: Identifies which rare defects actually dominate recombination.
key_works: A. Alkauskas, Q. Yan, and C. G. Van de Walle (2014), [First-principles theory of nonradiative carrier capture via multiphonon emission](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.90.075202).

title: Spatial hot-phonon bottleneck inversion
open: Infer local carrier and phonon distributions without confusing transport with changing spectra. Predict when phonon reabsorption produces expanding, contracting, or non-Gaussian carrier profiles.
status: Longstanding; 2024 MoS₂ microscopy resolved expansion, apparent negative diffusion, and subsequent expansion, leaving transferable microscopic inversion open.
why: Replaces misleading single-temperature descriptions of energy flow.
key_works: X. Wei et al. (2024), [Unveiling Spatiotemporal Diffusion of Hot Carriers Influenced by Spatial Nonuniform Hot Phonon Bottleneck Effect in Monolayer MoS2](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c02059).

title: The Ta2NiSe5 excitonic order parameter
open: Establish whether electron–hole pairing drives the Ta₂NiSe₅ transition, follows lattice distortion, or forms inseparable cooperative order. A decisive experiment must distinguish these possibilities beyond observing a gap.
status: The excitonic-insulator proposal dates to the 1960s; 2025 measurements still address competing electronic and lattice interpretations.
why: Establishes when excitonic insulation is a distinct thermodynamic phase.
key_works: N. Maraytta et al. (2025), [Unveiling excitonic insulator signatures in Ta2NiSe5 through structural and orbital probes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-20909-7).

title: Carrier-mediated ferromagnetism in dilute wide-gap nitrides
open: Demonstrate homogeneous dilute magnetic nitrides with reproducible, carrier-controlled ferromagnetism above room temperature, excluding precipitates and secondary phases. Establish the exchange mechanism using complementary probes.
status: Pursued since around 2000; established low-temperature functionalities do not establish this combined high-temperature target.
why: Connects electrical carrier control with robust magnetic functionality.
key_works: T. Dietl and H. Ohno (2014), [Dilute ferromagnetic semiconductors: Physics and spintronic structures](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.187); [arXiv:1307.3429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3429).

title: Affordable native GaN substrates
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Produce larger native GaN wafers with low defect density, controlled conductivity, and usable yield at costs supporting widespread vertical devices.
status: Commercial substrates exist; cost and quality barriers persist from the 2018 roadmap into a 2026 assessment.
why: Reduces defects and mismatch in vertical structures.
key_works: H. Amano et al. (2018), [The 2018 GaN power electronics roadmap](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6463/aaaf9d); R. Shankari et al. (2026), [Vertical gallium nitride MOSFETs: Advanced architectures, fabrication technologies, and performance breakthroughs for high-power applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mee.2025.112418).

title: Useful p-type beta-Ga2O3
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Demonstrate reproducible mobile-hole transport with useful density and mobility, or establish practical self-trapping and compensation limits.
status: Longstanding; the 2024 review establishes no useful bipolar conductivity.
why: Enables native p–n junction functionality.
key_works: J. L. Lyons, D. Wickramaratne, and A. Janotti (2024), [Dopants and defects in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cossms.2024.101148).

title: Atomic assignment of electrically active Ga2O3 defects
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Assign measured trap families to vacancies, impurities, complexes, and local structures, including charge states and capture cross-sections. Reconcile spectroscopy, calculations, growth chemistry, and irradiation.
status: Active since electronic-grade Ga₂O₃ emerged; McCluskey’s 2020 tutorial documents both established behavior and incomplete assignments.
why: Enables reproducible compensation and leakage control.
key_works: M. D. McCluskey (2020), [Point defects in Ga2O3](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5142195); [author publication list](https://labs.wsu.edu/mccluskey/publications/articles2020/).

title: Stable low-resistance contacts to n-type diamond
open: Produce uniform electron-injecting contacts surviving high temperature and current, while separating contact barriers from bulk donor freeze-out.
status: Decades old; elevated-temperature n-channel demonstrations leave substantial injection and bulk-resistance constraints.
why: Prevents contacts from dominating power losses.
key_works: Liao et al. (2024), [High-Temperature and High-Electron Mobility Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors Based on N-Type Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202306013).

title: Efficient bulk p-type AlN
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Achieve reproducible bulk hole conduction with adequate activation, low compensation, and preserved crystal quality. Identify the actual transport mechanism.
status: Pursued for decades; a 2024 review describes renewed Be-doping progress alongside incorporation, acceptor-depth, and solubility constraints.
why: Enables bipolar ultrawide-gap nitride structures.
key_works: T. Wostatek et al. (2024), [Ammonothermal Crystal Growth of Functional Nitrides for Semiconductor Devices: Status and Potential](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17133104).

title: Polarization-free high-flux CdZnTe
open: Maintain uniform fields, stable collection, and low leakage in thick CdZnTe under intense irradiation. Control both bias-induced and radiation-induced trap charging over large areas.
status: Studied for decades; high-flux material and 2024 XIDer experiments improve performance, but trapping and time-dependent leakage persist.
why: Enables detectors for intense next-generation light sources.
key_works: M. Collonge et al. (2024), [Probing the potential of CdZnTe for high-energy high-flux 2D X-ray detection using the XIDer incremental digital integrating readout](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphy.2024.1304570).

title: Sub-keV nuclear-recoil ionization yield
open: Measure and explain electron–hole production distributions from low-energy Si and Ge nuclear recoils, including thresholds and crystal orientation. Resolve conflicting measurements using traceable recoil calibration.
status: Decades old; a 2024 Ge experiment revisited 254 eV recoils after inconsistent earlier yields.
why: Controls interpretations of neutrino and light-dark-matter searches.
key_works: A. R. L. Kavner and I. Jovanovic (2024), [Measurement of ionization produced by 254 eV nuclear recoils in germanium](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.083043).

title: Nonmonotonic illumination drift in flexible IGZO
open: Predict and suppress threshold-drift reversal under combined negative bias, illumination, and heating. Transfer the model across thicknesses, spectra, and display duty cycles.
status: A longstanding oxide-backplane problem; 2025 work linked reversal to hydrogen/oxygen-associated states and suppressed it through thickness optimization.
why: Prevents brightness drift during low-refresh operation.
key_works: D. Kim, K.-B. Lee, and B. Choi (2025), [Hydrogen and oxygen induced abnormal reliability degradation in flexible top-gate amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O thin-film transistors under negative bias thermal illumination stress](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2025.106902).

title: Scandium segregation below the nominal phase boundary
open: Prevent nanoscale Sc-rich leakage paths while preserving switchable wurtzite AlScN. Predict precipitation from local composition fluctuations rather than average composition.
status: Sharpened by 2025 observations of metallic rocksalt precipitates and enhanced leakage even at 10% Sc.
why: Connects ferroelectric switching with predictable insulation.
key_works: D. Wu et al. (2025), [Atomic Origins of Leakage Paths in Epitaxial Al1−xScxN Thin Films](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03675).

title: Sub-10-nm low-resistance n-type contacts
open: Maintain reproducible ohmic injection through contacts shorter than 10 nm in integrated top-gated TMD transistors at logic voltages.
status: Central since the 2010s; 2025 antimony contacts reached 98 Ω·µm at 18-nm contact length and 40-nm contacted gate pitch.
why: Prevents contacts from consuming scaling benefits.
key_works: M. Du et al. (2025), [Scaled crystalline antimony ohmic contacts for two-dimensional transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01500-4).

title: Low-voltage 2D circuit speed beyond small oscillators
open: Demonstrate speed and energy benefits in large complementary circuits with realistic wiring, fan-out, and leakage at matched functionality and voltage.
status: Circuit integration has lagged devices since the 2010s; five-stage MoS₂ oscillators reached 2.65 GHz in 2023.
why: Establishes a useful computing technology.
key_works: D. Fan et al. (2023), [Two-dimensional semiconductor integrated circuits operating at gigahertz frequencies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01052-5).

title: Long-lived complementary CNT extension doping
open: Preserve selective CNT extension doping and matched complementary thresholds through processing and prolonged bias stress at scaled dimensions.
status: Sought since the 2000s; 2023 localized solid-state doping produced thresholds of +0.29 V and −0.25 V.
why: Enables stable complementary CNT logic.
key_works: Z. Zhang et al. (2023), [Complementary carbon nanotube metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors with localized solid-state extension doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01047-2).

title: Low-voltage ferroelectric tunnel-junction margins
open: Combine large persistent electroresistance, low-voltage writing, endurance, and small-area uniformity in the same operating regime.
status: Explored since the 2000s; 2024 junctions achieved 1-nm barriers and billions of cycles, with contrast and endurance optimized under different pulses.
why: Makes extreme resistance ratios practically usable.
key_works: Y. Jia et al. (2024), [Giant tunnelling electroresistance in atomic-scale ferroelectric tunnel junctions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-44927-7).

title: Tenfold system-energy gain for autoregressive analogue inference
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Proposed target: reduce energy per generated token tenfold against matched digital hardware, including loading, nonlinear operations, and memory traffic at equal quality and latency.
status: Active since the 2010s; 2023 analogue hardware demonstrated multi-chip speech inference with 45 million weights.
why: Addresses utilization and movement costs in token generation.
key_works: S. Ambrogio et al. (2023), [An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5).

title: Sub-picojoule optical I/O including all overheads
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Deliver an optical I/O system below one picojoule per delivered bit counting lasers, drivers, receivers, tuning, coding, and idle overhead under realistic traffic and temperatures.
status: Active for over a decade. Wan and colleagues' 2025 review describes component and co-design progress, but identifies sub-picojoule total-link energy and petabit integration as continuing system objectives.
why: Reduces the communication energy constraining distributed computing.
key_works: Wan et al. (2025, online), [*Integrating silicon photonics with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technologies*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44287-025-00223-0).

title: Tenfold lower EUV energy per yielding exposure
open: Proposed moonshot: reduce total electricity per good patterned wafer layer tenfold against a declared production baseline, holding pitch, defect yield, and throughput requirements fixed.
status: ASML demonstrated a 1,000 W EUV source in April 2025; its account distinguishes that milestone from a commercial source. Optical power alone does not establish energy per good wafer.
why: Reduces operating cost and the environmental burden of scaling.
key_works: ASML (2026), [“Strategy & stories,” 2025 Annual Report](https://www.asml.com/en/investors/annual-report/2025/strategy-and-stories).

title: Tenfold reduction of electrically reset PCM energy
open: Proposed target: lower RESET energy tenfold against a declared scaled baseline, preserving speed, retention, read margin, and endurance, including contact losses.
status: Thermal-confinement research spans decades; 2024 superlattice devices demonstrated approximately 0.7-V switching at 40-nm dimensions.
why: Reduces melt–quench energy costs.
key_works: X. Wu et al. (2024), [Novel nanocomposite-superlattices for low energy and high stability nanoscale phase-change memory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42792-4).

title: Manufacturable sub-0.01-square-micrometre CFET SRAM
open: Fabricate CFET SRAM below 0.01 μm² per bitcell with usable read/write margins, routable arrays, and demonstrated statistical yield. Include local interconnect resistance and transistor mismatch in measured macro performance.
status: A 2020s scaling target; Abdi's 2025 design–technology study predicts sub-0.01 μm² cells and improved write margins using wordline folding, rather than demonstrating a manufactured memory array.
why: SRAM area scaling increasingly constrains cache capacity and processor cost.
key_works: Dawit B. Abdi et al. (2025), [*SRAM Scaling Opportunities Below 0.01 μm² Using Double-Row CFET Architecture with Wordline-Folded Bitcell Design for Performance Optimization*](https://www.vlsisymposium.org/wp-content/uploads/VLSI2025_Advanceprogram0418.pdf).

title: High-temperature single-exposure dynamic range without noisy gain transitions
open: Achieve flicker-free single-exposure dynamic range above 130 dB, with transition signal-to-noise ratio above 30 dB at 125 °C in approximately 2-µm pixels.
status: Pursued since the 1990s. Innocent reported 126-dB test-chip range in 2025; their product target sacrificed range to preserve high-temperature transition quality.
why: Preserves automotive lamp and shadow detail.
key_works: Innocent et al. (2025), [*2.1µm LFM Automotive Pixel with Single Photodiode and 126 dB of Single Exposure Dynamic Range*](https://doi.org/10.60928/es6a-7h7l).

title: Increasing-distance quantum error correction in silicon
open: Demonstrate repeated silicon error correction with logical error rates decreasing as code distance increases, including leakage, measurement errors, and parallel operation.
status: Pursued since spin-qubit proposals. In 2026, donor clusters implemented a [[4,2,2]] detection code and shuttled spins performed weight-four parity checks; scalable error suppression remains unestablished.
why: Converts high-quality physical spins into dependable computational resources.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Universal logical operations in a silicon quantum processor*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-026-02140-1); Undseth et al. (2026), [*Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10766-3).
